_note: Order Up, the phone game at /play (src/play.njk, assets/js/play.js). Everything a non-programmer might want to change is here: the foods, the tickets, the specials, the items and their odds, the family's small talk, and the numbers that set how hard a day is. The rules these follow are in game/README.md. play.11tydata.js checks every `menu` name against menu.json when the site builds and warns if one has gone, so the game can't serve something the café stopped selling.
_note_parts: Every food a plate can hold. `cook` (seconds on the flat-top) makes it a food that cooks: it goes on the griddle first and must be pulled when done. No `cook` and it goes straight on the plate. `sprite` is the drawing in partials/game/sprites.njk (s-<sprite>). `raw` and `raw2` are the colours it shows before it's done. `flip` makes it a food that must be turned half way through (on the levels that have flipping, see `levels`): it stops cooking at the half until it is flipped, and burns if it is left.
_note_bins: The twelve bins, four across, top row first. Bacon, tortilla and cheese keep their place when breakfast turns to lunch at 11am, so a thumb finds them again. The bottom row is the same all day; soup, side and special open at 11am and the roll only with the Cinnamon Roll Case.
_note_recipes: The tickets. `name` is what the ticket says, `menu` the item in menu.json it stands for (left out for something that isn't on the printed menu), `parts` what goes on the plate (four at most; a pickle spear can always be added at lunch for a better tip, so it is never listed), `when` breakfast or lunch, `tier` 1 to 3 (Monday serves tiers 1 and 2; tier 3 comes in from Wednesday), and `photo` the café's own picture for the Recipe Box.
_note_specials: The dawn pick: three of these are offered each morning. All were real specials with their real sides (the weekly posts). One side is a quicker plate; two sides tips more. A special is held hot, so nothing on it cooks: special, then a side for each side named.
_note_catering: Friday's catering order: these platters, one after another, on one clock.
_note_items: Gear and tricks. After close the player picks one of three for free, then may buy from three more; both are dealt by `rarity` using `odds` below. `price` is tips. `max` is how many can be owned (1 when left out). `icon` is a sprite. What each one DOES is in play.js under the same `id`; `text` only says it, so keep the two in step.

_note_odds: The chance of each rarity when a card is dealt (Legendary is never dealt: the Deep Fryer turns up by itself as a fourth card, legendaryChance out of 100 each time the shop is stocked, at a price no week can reach; owner 2026-11-12: it must be a lucky sight, not a regular one). Rares come up more than they used to (owner 2026-11-12), but items only help: the score is the tips a week keeps, so a Rush week won with few items is the best kind, by which close it is (Monday's first). They must add up to 100. A rarity with nothing left to offer falls back to the one below it.
_note_skip: After close the free item can be turned down for tips instead (owner 2026-11-12): `bonus` is the tips by which close it is (Monday's first). More later in the week, when an item has fewer days left to pay for itself. Counted in tips earned, so it adds to the score.
_note_sale: A week that has bought nothing in the shop by `fromDay`'s close (0 = Monday, so 2 = Wednesday's) has `chance` out of 100, at each close from then on, of finding everything `off` percent cheaper (owner 2026-11-12: by Thursday an item has little time left to pay off, and the prices were out of reach). Prices round to $5. Not the Deep Fryer.
_note_days: How hard each day is. `every`: seconds between tickets. `patience`: multiplies how long a ticket waits. `tier`: the hardest ticket that can come in. `family`: the chance, out of 100, that family comes by at lunch. `burn`: seconds done food lasts before it burns.
_note_tuning: dayLength: seconds a shift takes. breakfastShare: the part of it before 11am. cups: coffees a day. rail: tickets that fit. waitBase + waitPerPart x parts: seconds a ticket waits. lateAt: the share of its time left when a ticket turns red. toGo: chance out of 100 a lunch ticket is to go. specialShare: chance out of 100 a lunch ticket is the special. fair: what keeps a hard day from being an impossible one. A ticket never waits less than cookTimes x its longest cook + perPart seconds a part + base. With bigAtOnce tickets of bigParts parts already up, the next one is a small one. After a walk-out the tickets still up get breath more seconds and nothing new comes for breathHold seconds.
_note_levels: How hard, picked on the title screen and kept for the whole week. `flip`: none (food never needs turning), tap (a tap or a swipe turns it) or swipe (only a swipe does). `wait` multiplies how long every ticket waits, `every` the seconds between tickets (bigger is slower), `burn` how long done food lasts. `family` multiplies each day's family chance in `days` (0 is never); `familyFloor` is a chance out of 100 that applies from Tuesday whatever the day says. The best week is kept for each level by itself.

easy.name: Easy
easy.text: No flipping, no distractions, tickets wait longer.

normal.name: Regular
normal.text: Flip eggs and burgers with a tap. Things get busy by Wednesday.

hard.name: Rush
hard.text: Flip with a swipe. Shorter waits. More going on, sooner.

_note_family: Family at the counter (Wednesday on, see `days`; never on Easy and sooner on Rush, see `levels`). The player is not warned: they just turn up when the week gets hard (owner 2026-11-11). They eat free, they wait a long time, and they talk: a line pops up over the kitchen every `every` seconds and stays until it's tapped. Feed them and they pour you a coffee back (or leave $`leave` if none is spilled); `cookieChance` out of 100 they brought a cookie. Words only, never a face, and no real names. Keep the lines kind: this is somebody's mother.
